title: How Millwork Companies in Canada Can Reduce Taxes and Improve Cash Flow With Strategic Tax Planning

rows.before: Ontario reduced its small business rate to 2.2% effective 1 July 2026, giving a blended provincial rate near 2.7% for a calendar-year corporation and a combined rate near 11.7% rather than the 12.2% that applied before.
rows.after: Ontario reduced its small business rate to 2.2% effective 1 July 2026, giving a blended provincial rate near 2.7% for a calendar-year corporation and a combined rate near 11.7% rather than the 12.2% that applied before.
rows.note: 12.2% expressly tied to the period before the July 1, 2026 cut; leave as is.

rows.before: Incorporated millwork companies get a federal small business deduction limit of $600,000 starting 2026. This reduces federal taxes on active business income below that amount. Watch out though:
rows.after: Incorporated millwork companies get a federal small business deduction limit of $500,000 starting 2026. This reduces federal taxes on active business income below that amount. Watch out though:
rows.note: Federal SBD limit stated as $600,000; correct to $500,000. The Risk Warning callout immediately after ("is $500,000, not $600,000") then becomes redundant; Sharad may wish to delete that callout.

rows.before: The federal small business deduction limit is $500,000, not $600,000. The higher figure belongs to the provincial limits in Saskatchewan, Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia. Please plan against $500,000 federally.
rows.after: The federal small business deduction limit is $500,000, not $600,000. The higher figure belongs to the provincial limits in Saskatchewan, Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia. Please plan against $500,000 federally.
rows.note: Contrasts $500,000 federal limit with $600,000 provincial figure; already correct, leave.

rows.before: $500,000 of active business income for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation, shared across associated corporations. The $600,000 figure belongs to the provincial limits in Saskatchewan, Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia.

rows.before: Please note that the federal business limit is $500,000 rather than $600,000; that the T5018 return is due six months after your reporting period ends rather than on 31 March; that records are retained for six years rather than seven; and that an eligible dividend is reported on a T5 rather than a TD1.
